mainTopic: אלמנת עיסה and how silence under accusation affects lineage, followed by the משנה of the girl attacked at the spring
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא about אלמנת עיסה, a widow from a family whose lineage is mixed and uncertain. רבי מאיר says he heard that a family with no doubt of ממזרות, נתינות or עבדי מלכים may marry into כהונה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, quoting רבי מאיר, says instead that the worry is a hidden ספק חלל, because people track ממזרים but not חללים. The גמרא asks three questions: why should חלל be treated differently, why does רבי מאיר repeat the תנא קמא, and how can the ברייתא contradict itself. רבי יוחנן answers that the argument is about a person who stays silent when accused. The תנא קמא counts any silence as an admission. In one report of רבי מאיר, silence about חלל means nothing. In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's report, only silence about ממזר means nothing. This also explains two ברייתות that rule in opposite ways on silence. Then a new משנה tells of a girl attacked at a spring, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי rules by the town's majority. רבא asks how that fits רבן גמליאל or רבי יהושע, and רב נחמן begins an answer from רב that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A family with none of these doubts may marry into כהונה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A family that has none of the listed doubts (ממזרות, נתינות, עבדי מלכים) is fit, and its widow may marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: I heard: any family that has none of all these problems, we allow her to marry into the priesthood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר, speaking in the ברייתא, reports a tradition he heard. If none of the doubts just listed applies to the family, its widow may marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'these' points back to the list in the ברייתא: doubts about ממזרות, נתינות and עבדי מלכים. A doubt about being a חלל is not on that list. So this view treats such a doubt as no obstacle to כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: I heard (a received tradition)
we marry off / allow to marry
the priesthood (marrying a כהן)
widow from a family of mixed, questionable lineage (like mixed dough)

phrases.english: I heard:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶחָד מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ —
phrases.english: any [family] that has none of all these [doubts]
phrases.notes: 'These' means the doubts listed just before in the ברייתא: ממזרות, נתינות and עבדי מלכים.

phrases.english: we let her marry into the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁמַעְתִּי, כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶחָד מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A family free of doubts about ממזרות, נתינות and עבדי מלכים may marry into כהונה, even if there is a doubt about חלל.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's report of רבי מאיר: the real worry is a hidden ספק חלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, quoting רבי מאיר and joined by רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, defines אלמנת עיסה as a widow from a family with a ספק חלל mixed into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר, and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא said the same: what is an אלמנת עיסה? Any family into which a doubtful חלל has been mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא gives a different definition of אלמנת עיסה. According to it, the problem is a doubtful חלל blended into the family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view reverses the first one. The first view ignored a doubt about חלל. Here, that doubt is exactly what makes the family questionable for כהונה. The word 'עיסה' (dough) fits, because the doubtful person is mixed in like ingredients in dough.

keyTerms.meaning: in the name of
in agreement with his words
was absorbed / blended in
a person who might be a חלל (unfit child of a כהן's forbidden marriage)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא
phrases.english: and likewise Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya would
say as he did:
Which is the widow of a mixed family?
Any [family] in which a doubtful חלל has blended in.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing definition that treats ספק חלל as the main concern, the opposite of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אלמנת עיסה is a widow from a family with a ספק חלל mixed in, and that doubt is what limits marriage into כהונה.

steps.title: The reason: ממזרים are known, חללים are not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains why a doubt about חלל is worse than a doubt about ממזר. The Jewish people keep track of ממזרים, but not of חללים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Jews recognize the ממזרים among them, but they do not recognize the חללים among them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reason behind the view reported by רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the name of רבי מאיר in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזר is publicly known, so there is little fear that one quietly slips into a good family. A חלל is not tracked, so he can blend in without anyone noticing. That is why the hidden ספק חלל is the real danger for כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: they recognize / identify
children of forbidden unions, who may not marry into the community
people unfit for כהונה because of a forbidden priestly marriage

steps.confusionAlert: A ממזר is the more severe status, but here the doubt about a חלל is treated as the bigger worry. The reason is that a חלל can go unnoticed, not that being a חלל is worse.

phrases.english: Jews recognize the ממזרים among them,
but they do not recognize the חללים among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for step 2's focus on ספק חלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People keep track of ממזרים but not of חללים, so only a hidden חלל threatens a family's fitness for כהונה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views of אלמנת עיסה. The first view (the תנא קמא, and רבי מאיר's own 'שמעתי') worries about ממזרות, נתינות and עבדי מלכים. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, reporting in the name of רבי מאיר, worries about ספק חלל, because חללים are not tracked.

steps.title: The גמרא infers from the first view: a doubt about חלל is fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first definition again and draws out what it implies: if the only doubt is about חלל, the family is fit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: what is an אלמנת עיסה? Any family that is not under a doubt of ממזרות, nor of נתינות, nor of royal slaves. This implies that a doubt about חלל is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finished, and the גמרא now begins analyzing it. It quotes the first view and reads an inference from it, setting up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list mentions only ממזרות, נתינות and עבדי מלכים. By leaving out חלל, the first view implies that a doubt about חלל does not disqualify. This inference stands in direct tension with רבי מאיר's view, and it prepares the next move in the סוגיא.

keyTerms.meaning: status of the נתינים (Gibeonite descendants, barred from marrying in)
royal slaves (doubtful status)
'this implies ... is fit': an inference drawn from what was left out

phrases.english: The Master said:
Which is the widow of a mixed family?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ לֹא מִשּׁוּם מַמְזֵרוּת,
phrases.english: Any [family] that has no [doubt] of ממזר status,
nor of נתין status,
nor of being royal slaves.
This implies: [a doubt of] חלל is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first view (step 1) and states its implication openly, setting it against רבי מאיר's view in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the first view, a family whose only doubt is about חלל is fit for כהונה.

steps.title: Why is a doubt about חלל different from the others?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Why should a doubt about ממזר or נתין disqualify the family while a doubt about חלל does not, if all of them are Torah-level flaws?
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes these flaws different? They come from the Torah, but a חלל also comes from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on what was just implied in step 4: that only a doubt about חלל leaves the family fit for כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ממזרות and נתינות are Torah-level flaws, and so is being a חלל. So why should a doubt about the first ones disqualify the family, but a doubt about חלל be ignored? The ברייתא seems to draw a line with no clear reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? The גמרא asks why two cases are treated differently.
From the Torah; a Torah-level law
These (the listed flaws)

phrases.english: What is different about these — that they are from the Torah,
phrases.notes: "These" means the flaws listed earlier, like ממזר and נתין.

phrases.english: a חלל is also from the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference drawn in step 4 that a doubtful חלל leaves the family fit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied ruling that a doubt about חלל does not disqualify the family.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All the flaws are equally Torah-level, so there is no clear reason to treat חלל more leniently.

steps.title: רבי מאיר seems to repeat the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: A second question: רבי מאיר says a family without any of these flaws is fit for כהונה. That sounds exactly like the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another problem: רבי מאיר said, 'I heard that any family that has none of these flaws, we may marry its widow to a כהן.' But that is just what the תנא קמא said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second question. רבי מאיר's statement seems to add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already said that a family free of ממזרות, נתינות and עבדי מלכים is fit. When רבי מאיר says the same thing, it sounds like no argument at all. The גמרא wants to know what the difference between them is.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, another difficulty
I heard (a tradition from my teachers)
That is the same as the first, unnamed opinion
We marry her off; she may be married

phrases.english: And furthermore, רבי מאיר said: I heard,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶחָד מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ
phrases.english: any family that has not even one of all these flaws,
we marry her into the כהונה,
phrases.notes: "Her" is the widow from that family.

phrases.english: that is the same as the first Tanna?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second difficulty alongside the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's statement in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His words match the תנא קמא, so there seems to be no argument between them.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא contradicts the beginning
steps.stepSummary: A third question: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר quotes רבי מאיר as saying that a doubtful חלל disqualifies the family. But the first part of the ברייתא said a חלל leaves it fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another problem: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר, and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא agreed: Which widow is an אלמנת עיסה? Any family that has a doubtful חלל mixed into it. People keep track of the ממזרים among them, but they do not keep track of the חללים. But in the first part you said a חלל is fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the later part of the ברייתא again, which steps 2–3 already explained. This time the purpose is to show that it contradicts the first part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part implied that a doubt about חלל does not disqualify a family. Here רבי מאיר is quoted as saying the opposite: a doubtful חלל mixed into a family is exactly what makes it a problem. The two parts of the same ברייתא seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say in the first part?
The first part of a teaching
Fit, acceptable

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: And furthermore: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר כִּדְבָרָיו:
phrases.english: and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא also used to say like his words:
Which is an אלמנת עיסה?
Any family into which a doubtful חלל has been mixed,
because the Jewish people recognize the ממזרים among them
but they do not recognize the חללים among them.
But you said in the first part that a חלל is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third difficulty, built on the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the ברייתא about חלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part is lenient about a doubtful חלל, but רבי מאיר, as quoted later in the same ברייתא, is strict about it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the argument is about staying silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the תנאים argue about a person who protests when called a ממזר but stays silent when called a חלל. The תנא קמא says silence about any flaw makes a person unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They argue about someone who shouts when called a ממזר but stays quiet when called a חלל. The תנא קמא holds that anyone who is called unfit and stays quiet is unfit. So this is what the תנא קמא means: Which family is fit for כהונה? Any family with no silence about ממזרות, no silence about נתינות, no silence about being עבדי מלכים, and no silence about being a חלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts answering by rereading the ברייתא. The real case is about people who are accused of a flaw and keep quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is not just a plain doubt. The ברייתא is talking about someone who was called a name and did not protest. According to the תנא קמא, staying silent counts as admitting the flaw, and this applies to every flaw, including חלל. So the תנא קמא is strict about a silent חלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shouts, protests loudly
Silent; silence (not protesting an accusation)
There is a difference between them; this is what they argue about
That people call him (a name)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַמְזֵר צוֹוֵחַ וְחָלָל שׁוֹתֵק
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said: one who shouts when called ממזר and is silent when called חלל —
that is the difference between them:
The first Tanna holds:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל פְּסוּל דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ וְשָׁתֵיק — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: any flaw that people call him and he stays silent — he is unfit.
And this is what the first Tanna is saying:
Which is an אלמנת עיסה?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ לֹא שְׁתוּק מַמְזֵרוּת,
phrases.english: any family that has no silence about ממזרות,
and no silence about נתינות,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שְׁתוּק עַבְדֵי מְלָכִים, וְלֹא שְׁתוּק חָלָל.
phrases.english: and no silence about being slaves of kings, and no silence about being a חלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַמְזֵר צוֹוֵחַ וְחָלָל שׁוֹתֵק אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the questions by redefining the case as one of silence after an accusation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (silence after being accused), which creates a real argument between the תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about plain doubts, so רבי מאיר appeared to repeat the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a silent accused person. The תנא קמא counts silence about every flaw, including חלל, as admitting it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read שְׁתוּק here as the שתוקי of the משנה in קידושין (a child whose father is unknown). Here it simply means someone who stayed silent when accused.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: silence about חלל does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers the תנא קמא. Silence only counts for flaws that would bar a person from marrying into the general community. Silence about חלל is meaningless, because he may simply not care.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר says to him: those flaws are the ones that would bar him from marrying into the community, so his silence about them counts. But silence about being a חלל leaves the family fit. The reason he stayed quiet is that he does not care.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his answer by explaining רבי מאיר's side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being called a ממזר, a נתין or an עבד מלך would stop a person from marrying almost anyone, so an innocent man would surely protest. Being called a חלל only matters for כהונה, so an innocent man might not bother to fight it. That is why רבי מאיר does not treat silence about חלל as admitting it. This also answers the first question: the flaws differ in how much a person cares about them.

keyTerms.meaning: Bars him from marrying into the community of Israel
He doesn't care
The congregation of Israel (for marriage purposes)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the תנא קמא and רבי מאיר argue about a man who stays silent when called a חלל. The תנא קמא says his silence counts as admitting it. רבי מאיר says his silence means nothing, because being a חלל only matters for כהונה and he may just not care.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how much weight silence carries as an admission. Silence is only meaningful when an innocent person would have been expected to protest.

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר says to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָנָךְ הוּא דְּקָא פָּסֵיל לֵיהּ בְּקָהָל,
phrases.english: those are the ones that disqualify him from the community,
phrases.notes: "Those" means ממזרות, נתינות and עבדי מלכים, so silence about them counts.

phrases.english: but silence about being a חלל — the family is fit.
And the fact that he is silent —
is because he does not care.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's answer by giving רבי מאיר's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the distinction (how much a person cares about the label).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All Torah-level flaws should be treated the same, and silence about any of them should count as admitting it.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, silence only counts for flaws that bar a person from the general community. Silence about חלל leaves the family fit.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version of רבי מאיר on silence
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר tells the תנא קמא that רבי מאיר only allowed silence about being called a ממזר, not silence about being called a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says to the first תנא who reported רבי מאיר's view: If you heard that רבי מאיר rules a person fit when he stays silent, it was not when they called him a חלל. It was when they called him a ממזר. He stays silent because he knows that being a ממזר is something people would already know about. But if they call him a ממזר and he protests loudly, or they call him a חלל and he stays silent, he is unfit. He stays silent about חלל because he feels it is enough that nobody is throwing him out of the Jewish community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third question from Step 7. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is not contradicting the first part of the ברייתא. He is reporting a different version of what רבי מאיר said about silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version the logic is the reverse of the תנא קמא's version. Staying silent about ממזר means nothing, because if it were true everyone would already know, so he does not bother to answer. Staying silent about חלל looks like an admission, because a חלל can still marry into the community and so he has a reason to let the charge pass.

keyTerms.meaning: He is silent; he does not protest
He screams in protest
It has a 'voice'; it would be publicly known
It is enough for him
They expel him from the community, meaning they bar him from marrying into it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the תנא קמא's version of רבי מאיר, silence about חלל is meaningless. In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version, silence about ממזר is meaningless and silence about חלל makes him unfit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the question from Step 7. The two parts of the ברייתא are not contradicting each other. They are two different reports of רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar is saying
to the first tanna who quoted Rabbi Meir:
If you heard
that Rabbi Meir rules a person fit in a case of silence
it is not where they called him 'chalal' and he was silent,
rather, where they called him 'mamzer' and he was silent.
And the reason this one is silent
is that he thinks: being a mamzer is something people would know about.
But if he is called mamzer and he screams in protest,
and called chalal and stays silent, he is unfit.
And the reason this one kept silent
is that he thinks: it is enough for him
that they do not throw him out of the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר לְתַנָּא קַמָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוחנן's explanation by giving רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version of רבי מאיר, which answers the question from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different reports of the same תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר seemed to contradict the first part of the ברייתא by saying a doubtful חלל makes the family unfit.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is talking about silence. In his version of רבי מאיר, silence about ממזר means nothing, but silence about חלל makes the person unfit.

steps.title: Two ברייתות contradict each other on silence
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא, quoting רבי יוסי, says silence about ממזר is fine and silence about חלל is not. Another ברייתא says the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says: a person who stays silent when called a ממזר is fit, but one who stays silent when called a חלל is unfit. Another ברייתא teaches: a person who stays silent when called a חלל is fit, but one who stays silent when called a ממזר is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that rule in opposite ways about silence. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות mirror each other exactly. Each one treats a different kind of silence as meaningful. The question is how both can be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in one ברייתא
Silent; one who stayed silent when accused
Fit / unfit

phrases.english: It is taught in one baraita: Rabbi Yosei says:
One who is silent when called mamzer is fit,
one who is silent when called chalal is unfit.
And it is taught in another baraita:
One who is silent when called chalal is fit,
one who is silent when called mamzer is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that two versions of רבי מאיר are on the table, the גמרא points to two ברייתות that clash in the same way.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each ברייתא treats the opposite kind of silence as meaningful, so they appear to contradict each other.

steps.title: Each ברייתא follows a different version of רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: No difficulty: one ברייתא follows the תנא קמא's report of רבי מאיר, and the other follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's report.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a difficulty. This ברייתא follows the תנא קמא's version of רבי מאיר, and that ברייתא follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction from Step 11. It uses the two versions of רבי מאיר we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that says silence about חלל is fine matches the תנא קמא's version (Step 9). רבי יוסי's ברייתא, which says silence about ממזר is fine, matches רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version (Step 10).

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
According to the view of

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reports of רבי מאיר's view on silence. In the תנא קמא's report of רבי מאיר, silence about חלל means nothing. In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's report, silence about ממזר means nothing, but silence about חלל makes a person unfit. רבי יוסי's ברייתא follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's report.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא תַּנָּא קַמָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: this one is the first tanna's version of Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: This is the second ברייתא, the one that says silence about חלל is fine.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: and this one is Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar's version of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי's ברייתא, the one that says silence about ממזר is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source follows a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא matches a different report of רבי מאיר's view, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: New משנה: the girl attacked at the spring
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells of a young girl who was attacked while drawing water. רבי יוחנן בן נורי rules that if most of the town's men may marry into כהונה, she may marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יוסי said: It once happened that a young girl went down to draw water from the spring, and she was raped. רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: If most of the people of the town marry their daughters into כהונה, then this girl may marry into כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a real case. A girl was attacked, and we do not know who the attacker was. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says we decide based on the majority of people in the town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the attacker may have been someone whose relations with her would make her forbidden to a כהן. רבי יוחנן בן נורי uses רוב: if most of the town is of a lineage that may marry into כהונה, we assume the attacker was one of them, so she is still fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
An actual incident that happened
A young girl
She was raped
Majority
The priesthood; marrying a כהן

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with a young girl
who went down to draw water from the spring,
and she was raped.
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
If most of the people of the town
marry their daughters into the priesthood,
then this girl may marry into the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is still about lineage and fitness for כהונה, but it moves to a new case of doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the attacker is unknown, we follow the majority of the town. If most may marry into כהונה, the girl may marry a כהן.

steps.title: רבא asks whose view רבי יוחנן בן נורי follows
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן. רבי יוחנן בן נורי's majority-based ruling does not fit רבן גמליאל, who permits even when most are unfit, or רבי יהושע, who forbids even when most are fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא said to רב נחמן: Whose opinion is רבי יוחנן בן נורי following? If he follows רבן גמליאל, then she should be allowed even when most of the town are unfit. If he follows רבי יהושע, then she should be forbidden even when most of the town are fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts discussing the girl at the spring. רבא asks how רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling, which depends on the majority, fits into the earlier מחלוקת between רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל trusts the woman's claim, so he permits her no matter what the town looks like. רבי יהושע does not trust her, so he forbids her no matter what. Neither one seems to care about the majority, so רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule appears to stand outside both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Which opinion does this follow?
A majority of people who are unfit to marry into כהונה
A majority of people who are fit to marry into כהונה
He rules her fit (permitted to marry a כהן)
He rules her unfit (forbidden to marry a כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying רבי יוחנן בן נורי is wrong. He is asking where his majority-based rule fits, since both sides of the earlier מחלוקת seem to ignore the majority.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rava said to Rav Naḥman:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי דְּאָמַר כְּמַאן?
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, who said this, follows whom?
phrases.notes: He means the ruling from the משנה in Step 13: if most of the town may marry into כהונה, she may too.

phrases.english: If he follows Rabban Gamliel,
then even where most are unfit, he should also rule her fit.
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל believes a woman who says her partner was fit, so the majority shouldn't matter to him.

phrases.english: If he follows Rabbi Yehoshua,
then even where most are fit, he should also rule her unfit!
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע doesn't trust her claim, so even a good majority wouldn't help her in his view.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי דְּאָמַר כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ruling of רבי יוחנן בן נורי in the משנה (Step 13) fits into the earlier מחלוקת of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling that the town majority decides whether she may marry a כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both known opinions ignore the majority. רבן גמליאל permits even with a bad majority, and רבי יהושע forbids even with a good majority. So a majority-based rule fits neither one.

steps.title: רב נחמן begins his answer by quoting רב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן starts to answer רבא by quoting a teaching that רב יהודה said in the name of רב. The content of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the answer. רב נחמן announces that he will quote רב יהודה in the name of רב, and the actual answer comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of answering in his own name, רב נחמן brings a tradition from רב. That teaching will show where רבי יוחנן בן נורי's majority rule fits.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he said (introduces a quoted teaching)
רב יהודה said in the name of his teacher רב

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here רב נחמן is the one answering רבא.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: This is what Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts רב נחמן's reply to רבא's question in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not stated yet. This line only introduces רב's teaching, which continues on the next amud.
